result: Zebrafish exhibit dark stripes of melanophores with light interstripes of xanthophores and iridophores, while pearl danio displays a nearly uniform pattern with fewer melanophores, more xanthophores, and intermingling of all three pigment cell classes.
evaluation: Claims C1 and C7 are directly stated and supported by Figure 1A showing the distinct pigment patterns of both species. Multiple citations support the characterization of these patterns, providing strong evidence for this descriptive result.

result: Prior work established that zebrafish pigment cells are neural crest-derived, iridophores specify stripe positions and promote xanthophore differentiation via Csf1, and interactions between melanophore and xanthophore lineages are required during stripe consolidation.
evaluation: Claims C2-C6, C28, and C87-C92 summarize established knowledge from prior research, all supported by multiple citations. These claims provide essential background context but represent prior work rather than novel findings from this study.

result: Zebrafish aox5+ cells of the xanthophore lineage extend long, fast projections with membraneous vesicles that reach 5-6 cell diameters, are especially frequent at early stripe formation stages (7-8 SSL), and are rare in pearl danio and among melanophores and iridophores of both species.
evaluation: Claims C8-C13 and C16-C18 are directly supported by time-lapse imaging data (Figure 1B-E, Videos 1-4) and quantitative comparisons (Figure 1C). The observations are well-documented with appropriate controls and statistical analysis showing species and cell-type specificity.

result: Fast projections contain both F-actin and tubulin, have highly meandering trajectories, carry vesicles of 1.7 ± 0.1 μm diameter (larger than cytoneme vesicles), exhibit transient EB3 accumulations suggesting active microtubule assembly, and are termed 'airinemes' based on their distinctive properties.
evaluation: Claims C19-C27 and C82-C83 are supported by multiple imaging approaches (Figure 2A-D, Video 5) using validated cytoskeletal markers. Quantitative measurements and comparisons to known structures (cytonemes, filopodia) are provided. The characterization is thorough and the naming is justified.

result: Airineme production is differentiation-state specific within the xanthophore lineage: unpigmented xanthoblasts in stripe regions extend more airinemes than pigmented xanthophores in interstripes, with xanthoblasts displaying membrane blebs from which airinemes originate.
evaluation: Claims C29-C34 are supported by spatial analysis (Figure 3B), high-resolution imaging (Figure 3C, Videos 6-7), and experimental manipulation of differentiation state using thyroid hormone (Figure 3D, Video 8). The interpretation of differentiation-state specificity is well-supported by converging evidence.

result: Airineme production by aox5+ cells is not markedly altered in mutants lacking melanophores or iridophores, or in transgenic fish with supernumerary melanophores.
evaluation: Claims C14-C15 are supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Video 2 showing airineme production persists across different genetic backgrounds. This control experiment demonstrates that airineme production is largely autonomous to the xanthophore lineage.

result: Airineme production depends on cytoskeletal components (inhibited by blebbistatin, nocodazole, and ML141/dnCdc42) and is required for melanophore stripe consolidation, as blocking airinemes with dnCdc42 in aox5+ cells causes ectopic melanophore persistence in the interstripe without affecting other cellular processes.
evaluation: Claims C35-C43 are supported by pharmacological inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B, Video 9), genetic manipulation with dnCdc42 (Figure 4A-B, Video 10), and comprehensive controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B-F). The specificity of the phenotype and preservation of other cellular functions strengthen the conclusion.

result: Airinemes exhibit target specificity, stabilizing on melanophores (especially embryonic and newly differentiating ones) but retracting rapidly from aox5+ cells, and deliver vesicles that persist on melanophores after airineme retraction.
evaluation: Claims C44-C49 are supported by dual-color time-lapse imaging (Figure 4C-E,G, Videos 11-14) showing differential stabilization times and target preferences. Quantitative analysis of stabilization on different cell types provides strong evidence for target specificity.

result: Airineme targeting specificity is genetically and evolutionarily labile: cx41.8 mutant zebrafish show later-appearing, more promiscuous airinemes that stabilize on both melanophores and xanthophores, as do the rare airinemes in pearl danio.
evaluation: Claims C50-C55 are supported by comparative analysis across genotypes and species (Figure 4D-F, Videos 15-16, Figure 4—figure supplement 4). The observation that targeting specificity can be altered by mutation or evolution is well-documented, though the mechanistic basis remains unclear.

result: Airinemes promote Delta-Notch signaling from xanthoblasts to melanophores: DlC is present in airineme vesicles, airineme inhibition reduces Notch-responsive melanophores, melanophore-specific Notch inhibition phenocopies airineme blockade, and genetic interactions support a model where airinemes transduce Delta-Notch signals that promote Kita-dependent melanophore rearrangements.
evaluation: Claims C56-C73 are supported by multiple converging lines of evidence: DlC localization (Figure 5A, Video 17), Notch reporter analysis (Figure 5B), genetic manipulations (Figure 5C-E), synergistic interactions (Figure 5E), and kita sensitization experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 5). The model is well-supported though alternative signaling mechanisms cannot be fully excluded.

result: Species differences in airineme production between zebrafish and pearl danio are non-autonomous to the xanthophore lineage and mediated by Csf1: zebrafish aox5+ cells in pearl hosts show reduced airineme production, and Csf1 overexpression in zebrafish reduces airineme frequency by 22% within 24 hr and 86% after complete xanthophore differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C74-C80 are supported by interspecific transplantation experiments (Figure 6A, Video 18, Figure 6—figure supplement 1) and Csf1 overexpression (Figure 6A, Video 19). The non-cell-autonomous nature of species differences and the role of Csf1 are well-demonstrated, though additional factors may contribute.

result: Airinemes represent a novel mode of long-distance cellular communication, and evolutionary changes in Csf1 expression in pearl danio drive precocious xanthophore differentiation, limiting both positional information to melanophores and airineme production, thereby altering pigment pattern.
evaluation: Claims C81 and C84-C86 represent the major conclusions synthesizing the experimental findings. The novelty of airinemes is supported by their distinct properties compared to known cellular projections. The evolutionary model for pearl danio is supported by transplantation and Csf1 manipulation data, though it remains a model requiring further validation.
